History of Present Illness:
___ year old man with CAD s/p CABG in ___ and h/o alcohol abuse 
p/w chest pain. He did not have any coronary events since his 
CABG. A few months again, he began to notice intermittent sharp 
left sided chest pain that comes on randomly lasting anywhere 
from hours to minutes. He takes nitro's with relief only 
sometimes. Today, he noted sharper than usual chest pain and 
decided to come to the ED for further evaluation. Of note, he 
had a recent normal stress test at ___ in ___. He also reports 
some mild SOB. There is no evidence of a pleuritic component to 
his chest pain. He admits to some PND over the past few nights 
which he explains is new for him. He states that he continues to 
smoke a pipe and has a long-standing h/o tobacco use. He also 
continues to drink alcohol, his last drink was on the day of 
admission, two screwdrivers. He has a h/o heavy alcohol use and 
has been hospitalized in the past for alcohol withdrawal but 
denied seizures. Denies orthopnea ___ edema.  
.  
He was evaluated earlier in ___, and ___ of this 
year and ruled out for MI. He was set up to see Dr. ___ in 
Cardiology for follow up but he missed his appointment. He has 
another appointment with Dr. ___ this month.  
.

98%RA. He received nitro and aspirin in ambulance. His EKG was 
unchanged and first set of cardiac markers were negative. He was 
also given a total of 6 mg of IV morphine for his chest pain.

Currently he does not have chest pain. He denies SOB, LH, 
palpitations.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old man with CAD, CVA, and alcohol abuse who presents 
with atypical chest pain.  
.  
# Atypical Chest pain:  Pt had no further episodes of chest 
discomfort during his hospitalization.  Pt was ruled out for MI 
by CEs on admission.  Stress MIBI was unremarkable.  He was 
continued on his home continue aspirin, plavix, statin.  It was 
noted that beta blocker has been held in the past for 
bradycardia.  He has an outpatient appt scheduled for ___.  
.  
# SOB: Pt has progressed in last 2 months from SOB with exertion 
(manually using wheelchair to getting out of bed) to SOB at 
rest.  He had no e/o of heart failure on physican exam, CXR and 
BNP is borderline.  There was not e/o pneumonia on his CXR.  His 
SOB improved with trial of nebulizers.  He does have 
long-standing h/o tobacco use and current pipe smoking with 
chronic cough.  He was started on empiric treatment for COPD and 
discharged on Advair, ipratropium, and albuterol inhaler.  O2 
sats were high ___ while resting but fell to 80% with exertion 
(driving wheelchair), and he was discharged on home O2.  Pt was 
consueled about tobacco cessation by primary team and social 
work, esp. with use of home O2.  He will follow up with 
Pulmonology Clinic with PFTs and his PCP ___.  
.  
# Alcohol abuse:  Pt was placed on CIWA scale upon admission 
without any serious withdrawal symptoms.  He was started on 
thiamine, folate, MVT.  Social work worked with the patient.  
Patient willing to enter outpatient program.  Social work will 
contact his outpatient social worker regarding these programs.
.  
# h/o CVA: Pt was continued on asa and plavix.
.  
# Hypothyroid: TSH was 7.6 with fT4 of 0.77.  Levothyroxine was 
titrated up from 88 to 100 mcg daily.  Pt will f/u with his PCP 
for ___ recheck in 6 weeks.

Discharge Instructions:
___ were admitted for chest pain and shortness of breath.  All 
your tests indicate that ___ did NOT have a heart attack.  ___ 
had a stress test that showed that your heart appears to be 
fine.  Your shortness of breath improved with nebulizer 
treatments, suggesting that ___ have chronic obstructive 
pulmonary disease from your smoking.  ___ were taught how to 
take inhalers by the nurses.  ___ will need to take these 
inhalers at home.  Your oxygen level decreased when ___ were 
wheeling in the hallways and ___ will need to have oxygen at 
home.  ___ will also need to follow up with Dr. ___ at 
___ and get lung tests as an outpatient.
.
___ thyroid was found to be low and your levothyroxine has been 
increased to 100 mcg a day.  Please follow up wtih Dr. ___ to 
repeat your TSH in 6 weeks.
.
Please continue the rest of your medications as prescribed.
.

lightheadedness, or any other concerning symptoms, please call 
your primary care physician ___ at ___ or go to 
the Emergency Department.
